title: Musée national Picasso-Paris: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works that keep recognition alive while altering anatomy, scale and materials.
introduction:
A saddle and a handlebar can become a bull without ceasing to be bicycle parts. That double recognition offers a useful entry into this selection. Picasso's painted figures also keep enough familiar signs to remain readable while their proportions, contours and viewpoints change.

There is no single direction from realistic youth to abstract maturity here. The observed weight of a seated child, the mass of a bather and an acrobat's implausible curve answer different pictorial problems. Works by Seurat and Courbet provide comparisons rather than steps in Picasso's development. Follow a recurring subject through the selection and ask what has been retained, what has been altered, and what the alteration allows the image to do.
visitNote: The museum changes its displays and lends works to exhibitions. Check its current programme before visiting; this is a selection from the collection rather than a room-by-room route.

books.title: Pablo Picasso: A Retrospective
books.author: Edited by William Rubin
books.note: MoMA provides a digitized copy of William Rubin's 1980 retrospective catalogue under Publications. Its long chronological survey helps place these sharply different works within Picasso's wider production.

works.title: Bathers on the Beach
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Bathers on the beach. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/bathers-on-the-beach-1928
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Blue water establishes the setting before the angular orange forms resolve into bathers. Picasso has removed much of the anatomy that would ordinarily explain a pose. Position and relative scale take over that work. The figures remain bodies because a few signs hold together, not because every limb has a convincing counterpart in a person standing on a beach.

works.title: Jacqueline with Flowers
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Jacqueline with flowers. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/jacqueline-with-flowers-1954
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Jacqueline's profile forms a firm edge against the blue ground. Flowering stems and patterned clothing introduce smaller, more irregular movements around that outline. The long neck keeps the head distinct from the busier area below. Rather than blending sitter and decoration into a single texture, the portrait allows her still contour to resist the surrounding pattern.

works.title: Seated Woman
works.credit: Seated Woman. WikiArt; Georges Seurat. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.license: Public domain
works.description: Seurat's figure becomes solid through the accumulation of dark marks. Where the marks thin out, the body approaches the lightness of the paper instead of meeting a continuous boundary. This is a useful counterpoint to Picasso's emphatic contours elsewhere in the guide: a seated body can be established by changing density without first enclosing it in a line.

works.title: The Barefoot Girl
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. The barefoot girl. WikiArt source label: Public domain US. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/the-barefoot-girl-1895
works.license: Public domain US (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Folded hands and exposed feet anchor the upright girl in her seat. Her red dress separates her from the dark foliage, but the pose remains unshowy. This early work establishes how much Picasso could obtain from a sustained, relatively conventional portrait. Later distortions need not be read as an escape from an inability to describe weight or bodily proportion.

works.title: Bull's Head
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Bull's Head. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/bulls-head-1942
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The museum identifies the materials as an actual leather saddle and metal handlebar. Their earlier use remains easy to recognise: the narrow saddle becomes a muzzle, the curving handlebar becomes horns. Nothing needs to be disguised with realistic fur or modelled eyes. The sculpture holds together two identifications, allowing a bicycle and a bull to occupy the same small arrangement.

works.title: Head of a Goat
works.credit: Gustave Courbet. Head of a goat. Image credit: Gustave Courbet. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.license: Public domain
works.description: Courbet approaches an animal head by describing its particular anatomy. Light catches the eye and muzzle beneath the sweep of the horns; mountain and sky give the head a setting. Beside Picasso's assembled bull, the difference is instructive. One image specifies flesh and texture, while the other recruits existing objects. Both depend on the recognisability of a few relations.

works.title: Bust of a Woman in a Striped Hat
works.catalogueTitle: Buste de femme au chapeau rayé
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Bust of woman. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/bust-of-woman-1939
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Stripes do not stop at the border between costume and person. They help divide the woman's face and clothing, while the background continues the vertical rhythm. The features remain identifiable but no longer occupy a smoothly continuous surface. Picasso makes pattern an active part of the body's construction rather than decoration placed on an already completed likeness.

works.title: Two Nude Women on the Beach
works.catalogueTitle: Deux Femmes nues sur la plage
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Two naked women on the beach. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/two-naked-women-on-the-beach-1937
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The women's attention is directed downwards, but their enlarged limbs dominate the shallow space. A modest shared activity acquires the weight of a monumental grouping. The pressure between rounded forms is more important than a roomy setting: there is little opportunity for the eye to pass around the bodies. Closeness becomes a matter of physical construction.

works.title: Sleeping Woman with Shutters
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Sleeper near the shutters. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/sleeper-near-the-shutters-1936
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Head, arm and shoulder fold into a compact sequence of curves. Behind them, the shutters introduce a more regular system of lines. That contrast helps distinguish the sleeper's relaxed position from the room containing her. The figure need not obey ordinary anatomy in every detail for the familiar action of resting a head on an arm to remain clear.

works.title: Child Playing with a Truck
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Child playing in camomilles. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/child-playing-in-camomilles-1953
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The toy occupies little space within the busy arrangement of branches and leaves. Yet the child's bent posture gives it a claim on the whole scene: the body directs attention towards the truck. Picasso surrounds that small concentration with restless marks. The contrast preserves a recognisably absorbed activity without making the rest of the painting equally quiet.

works.title: Women in an Interior
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Woman in the interior. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/woman-in-the-interior-1936
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The figures do not fit the room by a single consistent measure. One sits with a book; the larger striped body presses against angled furniture and walls. Instead of correcting that disparity into a plausible interior, Picasso uses it to distinguish ways of occupying space. Domestic familiarity survives even as the room's dimensions become difficult to reconstruct.

works.title: Figure and Profile
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Figure and profile. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/figure-and-profile-1928
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Several eyes complicate the attempt to read the central outline as one face in one position. The open window nearby is much easier to identify. That ordinary object establishes a standard of legibility against which the figure becomes stranger. The image does not require a final choice between its possible facial readings; their coexistence is part of its structure.

works.title: Large Bather with a Book
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Great bather reading. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/great-bather-reading-1937
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The book is small beside the body bent around it. Broad limbs have something of stone's compactness, yet their arrangement communicates the everyday act of reading. Picasso gives concentration a physical enclosure: the massive figure gathers around a modest area of pages. The disproportion makes the activity more conspicuous rather than allowing the body to overwhelm it entirely.

works.title: Large Still Life on a Pedestal Table
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Great Still life on pedestal. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/great-still-life-on-pedestal-1931
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The objects compete for more space than a tidy tabletop view would allow. Curved outlines run across coloured areas, alternately separating vessels and joining them. Recognition happens locally, a shape at a time, rather than from one dependable viewpoint. The pedestal table provides a subject and an organising constraint, but not a stable little stage for independent objects.

works.title: The Acrobat
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Female acrobat. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/female-acrobat-1930
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The action takes precedence over anatomical plausibility. Picasso stretches the pale body into a long loop, then uses hands and feet to keep that turn readable as a human pose. The grey ground leaves the bending contour exposed. Tracing it reveals a body organised around continuity of movement rather than the ordinary limits of its joints.

works.title: Child with Doves
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. A child with pigeons. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/a-child-with-pigeons-1943
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Angular furniture fills much of the room around the small child. Pale birds carry attention upwards, while the rounded body remains low within this crowded framework. Differences of scale prevent the grouping from settling into an easy domestic scene. The child's enclosure is visible in the arrangement itself; it does not require an invented account of what the child feels.

works.title: Straw Hat with Blue Foliage
works.catalogueTitle: Le Chapeau de paille au feuillage bleu
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. The straw hat with blue leaves. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/woman-in-a-straw-hat-1936
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The hat has more elaborate incident than the face beneath it. Loops and blue leaves spread above a profile described through a few bounded areas of black, cream and violet. Picasso distributes detail selectively. The portrait remains identifiable without making every part equally informative, and the extravagant headwear gains force from the economy of the facial signs.

works.title: Paul as Harlequin
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Paul as harlequin. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/paul-as-harlequin-1924
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: The diamond costume makes Paul a performer, but his carefully described face and hands keep the portrait attached to a particular child. Less resolved areas around the lower furniture expose a difference in attention across the surface. The theatrical role does not absorb the sitter completely. Costume, likeness and the uneven degree of finish remain separately visible.

works.title: Massacre in Korea
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Massacre in Korea. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/massacre-in-korea-1951
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: A strip of open ground divides exposed women and children from armed figures. That interval is essential: the two groups face one another, but they do not possess comparable means of action. Mechanical-looking weapons intensify the imbalance. The painting's protest emerges from this organisation of force and vulnerability, without needing the figures to resemble a photographic report of a particular moment.

works.title: Maya with a Doll
works.credit: Pablo Picasso. Portrait of Maya with her doll. WikiArt source label: Pablo Picasso Fair Use. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pablo-picasso/portrait-of-maya-with-her-doll-1938
works.license: Pablo Picasso Fair Use (WikiArt source label)
works.description: Maya's large head and differently directed features complicate the portrait, while the doll makes her activity immediately familiar. Repeated colours connect the toy to the dress and sitter. The altered anatomy does not remove the relation between a child and an object held close. It changes how that companionship occupies the compact picture rather than replacing it with an abstract puzzle.

closingSections.title: Follow one transformation
paragraphs: Compare the hands in the early portrait, the beach figures and the acrobat. Each must do a different job. This selection is not a promised display route; consult the museum's current information for works available during your visit.
